title: Crawfishing and fishing in boyhood
summary: He caught crawfish in the canal and fished at Lake Pontchartrain, selling them; people cooked at home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, let me get my stuff together and you can just talk. I was going to ask you about things like hunting and crawfishing kind of here in the old days.

Well, I can recall when I used to go and meet my daddy at Lake Punching Train. I know you asked me just now was I ever afraid. I said no. I'd go through the woods. I'd go and meet him at Lake Punching Train and go fishing and come on. That's after I delivered my papers. Crawfish, I used to go catch them back at old Jordan Avenue Canal and be among the thousand snakes. And these old, they call them water mugs, these cotton mugs. And I'd go ahead and catch my crawfish and carry my sacks and my nets out and come on out and peddle them off. That was another means of making a few knickers to run the house.
Let me get my neck down and my coat to be ready to roll. Yeah, alright.
Did people go out to restaurants ever then and take a bus?
Not like it is now. Everybody cooked their own meals at the house and everybody was a good cook.
